text:
linus: Heads up — planning a kernel + GPU driver patch on cluster-gpua (us-east1). Need to pause autoscaling and evacuate nodes for the update. Proposed window: Tue 2026-03-24 03:00-05:00 UTC. Any blockers?

maria: Ack. Can you quantify impact? how many nodes/racks and expected capacity loss?

linus: Rough numbers: ~20 nodes across 3 racks (~150 GPUs total). Expect ~30% of serving capacity in us-east1 to be unavailable during peak of the window. This is a planned, staged evacuation (not all nodes at once).

nate: Thanks. We should pre-warm us-west2 and eu-north1 routing to absorb bursts. Also need to check Dedicated customer mapping — some reserved capacity might be in us-east1. @maria can you confirm any Dedicated mappings?

maria: Will check Dedicated map. Quick note: two enterprise tenants have hard region pins in us-east1 (acct-342, acct-198). They'll need explicit notice + potential temporary routing waiver.

ops-bot: Scheduling note: incident-runbook v2 will auto-create a maintenance incident and post status updates. To proceed, add the tag `cluster:gpua-maint` to the scheduled job.

linus: Evacuation plan (short): 1) Pause autoscaler for gpua pools 2) Drain nodes with `--ignore-daemonsets` and `--delete-local-data` 3) Reboot/apply driver + kernel patch 4) Rejoin and verify GPU health + nvlink tests 5) Gradual unpause autoscaler. Example drain command:

```
kubectl drain gpu-node-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

sophia: Cost question — pre-warming extra instances in other regions will incur transient cloud spend. Could we use short-lived spot pre-warm and then fallback to reserved if spots fail? That balances cost vs risk. :money_with_wings:

linus: Good call. Plan: pre-warm a mix: 30% reserved burst (already in budget), 70% spot. We'll set an aggressive scale-in policy post-window. I'll add budget tags.

oncall-uk: Heads-up — there's a separate infra task scheduled in us-east1 earlier that day (storage firmware check at 01:00-02:00 UTC). We should avoid overlapping IO-heavy work. Can we shift this window to 05:00-07:00 UTC instead?

linus: I saw that — thanks. Moving to 05:00-07:00 UTC would push us into some customer active hours for APAC; tradeoffs. Proposal: shift by +2h to 05:00-07:00 UTC but split the work across two nights (half nodes Tue night, half Wed night) to reduce surface. Thoughts?

maria: Splitting is safer. Also we need to publish a customer notice 72h in advance and update status page. I can draft both. Suggested blurb for status: "Planned kernel/driver upgrades for GPU cluster in us-east1; short interruptions to GPU-backed endpoints possible; failover to other regions expected."

linus: Love that blurb. Add a note about Dedicated tenants — we'll reach out individually. Action items: @maria publish notices + update ops playbook; @nate pre-warm us-west2/eu-north1 and run smoke tests; @sophia confirm budget and spot strategy; @oncall-uk verify no overlap with other maintenance. I'll put a canary on a single rack first night.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline scheduled: `infra/maintenance/gpua-kernel-update` -> run at 2026-03-24T05:00:00Z. Status: scheduled.

maria: Draft notice posted to #customer-comm-drafts, assigning legal review. Please review and suggest edits.

linus: Final decision: split across Tue/Wed 05:00-07:00 UTC, canary Rack-A Tue, Rack-B Wed. Evacuation play, fallback regions pre-warmed, Dedicated customers notified. If no further objections by EOD UTC I'll lock the schedule and run the pre-warm on Mon. :white_check_mark:

nate: ACK — I'll kick off pre-warm runbook Monday 22:00 UTC and post smoke logs.

sophia: ACK on budget plan. I'll watch spend and set alert thresholds.

oncall-uk: ACK — no conflicts from my side.

linus: Thanks everyone. I'll update the maintenance incident and attach the runbook. Please ping me directly if you spot anything we missed. :rotating_light:
